findings.reason: naming the existing provenance write lets §2 extend the one owner (the run/plan/ledger reason record) and reuse it rather than invite a second override-provenance path that drifts from `--no-fence`.
findings.text: §2 presents "a flag whose reason is recorded on the run and reaches the ledger row" as a new mechanism, but `--no-fence REASON` already does exactly that (cli.py:1815 `no_fence_reason`; dispatch.py:6904-6920, whose comment states the reason "is recorded on the run, its composed plan and its ledger row"), and the plan cites neither it nor the sibling override family (refusals.py D11 `--allow-unreconciled-runs`, D13/D18/D19 `--no-watch`, D23 `--allow-unreviewed-plan`) as prior art

findings.reason: the registry is the owner the refusal-visibility test and the refusal census read, so a discharge that never enters it is invisible to both and the two remedies will drift as the fence changes severity between recorded and refused.
findings.text: the fence composes its "discharge" as a bespoke string inside `_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop` (dispatch.py:4416-4456) with no family id registered, while `reckon/crew/refusals.py` owns "render crew refusals with the command that resolves them" through `DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES` and `format_refusal`, so §2's override and §4's move-to-refusal would add a second remedy surface beside the registry

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is added; the fence is composed in dispatch resolution as one small stop mapping (`_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop`) that reuses `resolve_role_override` to enumerate discharge candidates, so the behaviour sits behind the existing dispatch interface rather than behind parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the fence's discharge is composed inline in `_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4399) instead of extending `reckon/crew/refusals.py`, the module that owns discharge rendering and the refusal census.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 describes a reason-recording override as new, while `--no-fence REASON` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6904) already records an override's reason on the run, plan and ledger row, and is cited nowhere in the plan.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only new interface §2 adds is one CLI flag, the established override-flag family pattern (`--no-watch`, `--allow-unreconciled-runs`, `--allow-unreviewed-plan`), and §2 states why the override must exist and be recorded rather than taken by a config edit, so the layer is justified rather than a silent parallel to an extendable mechanism.
